analysis:
Reviewed all units. The only security-relevant runtime change is console-ui/src/lib/chat/stream.ts (head lines 226-235): after optional unsealing and JSON parse, a top-level `error` event is terminal. It dispatches the promotion-usage event, calls onError with `Stream failed: <message>` and returns without onDone or processing later deltas. This sits inside the try block, so `return` is not swallowed by the catch. Error handling occurs after unsealing, so sealed-stream behavior (TB-001, A-001) is unchanged. Decryption failure still fails closed.

The message is attacker-influenceable (provider or coordinator, ADV-001) and is passed as a string to a callback. The XSS risk depends on downstream rendering in useChatStream/UI, which was not supplied. React text rendering is likely safe, but this is unverified and pre-existing in kind (T-019 context). The change also stops delivery of content after an error, which reduces the risk that failed output is shown as complete. No new trust-boundary, auth, billing or attestation behavior was introduced.

A possible subtle edge: any chunk with a truthy `error` field aborts the stream, including a provider-supplied one, but a provider can already terminate or corrupt its own stream, so there is no new capability. The other files are a changelog, docs, a test fixture type update (GlobalWithdrawModal.test.tsx adds account_id and stripe_account_id fixture fields, which are fake values) and new tests with fixture keys only (tweetnacl keypair generated at test time). No secrets are present. No findings.
